title: Johan Fegraeus → (Ludwig Camerarius), Helsingør 11 and 21 July 1632, partly in cipher with the decipherment beside it
correspondents: Johan Fegraeus (Swedish agent at Helsingør) → Ludwig Camerarius
shelfmark: Munich, Bayerische Staatsbibliothek, Clm 10406 (Collectio Camerariana vol. 56), n. 74 et 77
folio_note: n. 74 = MDZ scans 283-284: fol. 1 (scan 283) all clear German; fol. 2 (scan 284) has cipher in about 9 of 27 lines, dated 'Helsingör den 11 Julij 1632', signed 'Johan Fegraeus'. n. 77 (21 July) not located; Halm also lists an 'n. 77 aus Brüssel', so the numbers may be confused.
status: Halm, Verzeichniss der handschriftlichen Sammlung der Camerarii (1874), p. 131: "Schreiben von Joh. Fegraeus aus Helsingör vom 11 u. 21 Juli, z. Th. in Chiffern mit beigesetzter Auflösung". Decipherment written beside the cipher: a key source for other Fegraeus or Camerarius-network letters, e.g. the Riksarkivet cipher filed with Camerarius's letters of 1628 (R4284, in the repo, not broken). Not on DECODE (repo dumps have no BSB Clm 103xx). Image: https://www.digitale-sammlungen.de/en/view/bsb00116454?page=1 (IIIF https://api.digitale-sammlungen.de/iiif/presentation/v2/bsb00116454/manifest). Located by WAINUT on 3 Nov 2026, not read: a mixed system of 4-digit code numbers for words and names (1418, 1420, 1726, 1745, 2102, 2935, 3168, 3906 ...), 2-digit numbers for letters and letter-like signs for short words ('rr' = und, glossed twice). 3168 = 'Kön. Mt.' and 1745 = 'gute' twice each. Not Camerarius's 1621-22 code (3168 and 1420 fall in the wrong alphabetical places there). One draft pass of scan 284 only; the glosses are cramped and partly illegible on the microfilm.
why: Swedish intelligence from the Sound in the summer of Lützen; the key may bear on R4284.
